Armenian language.fact: Grammatically, early forms of Armenian had much in common with classical Greek and Latin, but the modern language has undergone many analytic transformations like modern Greek.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Examples of noun declension in _____ case the direct object takes is split based on animacy (a phenomenon more generally known as differential object marking)
Armenian language.fact: Examples of noun declension in Eastern Armenian Which case the direct object takes is split based on animacy (a phenomenon more generally called differential object marking).

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: The most distinctive feature of _____ is that it has undergone several phonetic mergers; these may be due to proximity to Arabic- and Turkish-speaking communities
Armenian language.fact: The most distinctive feature of Western Armenian is that it has undergone several phonetic mergers; these may be due to proximity to Arabic- and Turkish-speaking communities. The Middle Armenian variety used in the court of Cilician Armenia (1080–1375) provides a window into the development of Western Armenian, which came to be based on what became the dialect of Istanbul, while the standard for Eastern Armenian was based on the dialect around Mount Ararat and Yerevan.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Fortson notes that the modern standard as well has now attained a subordinate clausal structure that greatly resembles a _____ language
Armenian language.fact: The different dialects have experienced different degrees of language contact effects, often with Turkic and Caucasian languages; for some, the result has been significant phonological and syntactic changes. Fortson notes that the modern standard as well has now attained a subordinate clausal structure that greatly resembles a Turkic language.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Thus, the _____ dialect pronounces both (թ) and (դ) as [tʰ], and the (տ) letter as [d]
Armenian language.fact: Western Armenian has simplified the occlusive system into a simple division between voiced occlusives and aspirated ones; the first series corresponds to the tenuis series of Eastern Armenian, and the second corresponds to the Eastern voiced and aspirated series. Thus, the Western dialect pronounces both (թ) and (դ) as [tʰ], and the (տ) letter as [d].

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Armenian can be divided into two major dialectal blocks and those blocks into individual dialects, though many of the _____ dialects have become extinct due to the effects of the Armenian genocide
Armenian language.fact: Western Armenian has simplified the occlusive system into a simple division between voiced occlusives and aspirated ones; the first series corresponds to the tenuis series of Eastern Armenian, and the second corresponds to the Eastern voiced and aspirated series. Armenian can be divided into two major dialectal blocks and those blocks into individual dialects, though many of the Western Armenian dialects have become extinct due to the effects of the Armenian genocide.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Although Western and _____ are often described as different dialects of the same language, many subdialects are not readily mutually intelligible
Armenian language.fact: Although Western and Eastern Armenian are often described as different dialects of the same language, many subdialects are not readily mutually intelligible.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Nakhichevan-on-Don Armenians speak another Western Armenian variety based on the dialect of Armenians in Crimea, where they came from in order to establish the town and surrounding villages in _____ (
Armenian language.fact: Nakhichevan-on-Don Armenians speak another Western Armenian variety based on the dialect of Armenians in Crimea, where they came from in order to establish the town and surrounding villages in 1779 (Նոր Նախիջևանի բարբառ).

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: It was introduced around 405 AD by _____, an Armenian linguist and ecclesiastical leader, and originally contained 36 letters
Armenian language.fact: It was introduced around 405 AD by Mesrop Mashtots, an Armenian linguist and ecclesiastical leader, and originally contained 36 letters.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: Two more letters, օ (ō) and ֆ (f), were added in the _____
Armenian language.fact: Two more letters, օ (ō) and ֆ (f), were added in the Middle Ages.

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: This alphabet and associated orthography is used by most _____n speakers of Armenia and the countries of the former Soviet Union
Armenian language.fact: It was introduced around 405 AD by Mesrop Mashtots, an Armenian linguist and ecclesiastical leader, and originally contained 36 letters. During the 1920s orthography reform in Soviet Armenia, a new letter և (capital ԵՎ) was added, which was a ligature before ե+ւ, whereas the letter Ւ ւ was discarded and reintroduced as part of a new letter ՈՒ ու (which was a digraph before).

Armenian language.subject: Education in India
Armenian language.question: This table lists some of the more recognizable cognates that Armenian shares with English words descended from _____
Armenian language.fact: This table lists some of the more recognizable cognates that Armenian shares with English words descended from Old English.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The _____ was Ancient Greek goddess.
Artemis.fact: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Artemis (; Ancient Greek: Ἄρτεμις) is the goddess of hunting, the wilderness, wild animals, transitions, nature, vegetation, childbirth, care of children, and chastity. Artemis was the daughter of Leto and Zeus, and twin sister of Apollo.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The goddess _____ is her Roman equivalent
Artemis.fact: The goddess Diana is her Roman equivalent.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In most accounts, the twins were produced by an extramarital liaison, for which _____'s wife Hera forbade Leto from giving birth anywhere on solid land
Artemis.fact: Artemis was the daughter of Leto and Zeus, and twin sister of Apollo. In most accounts, the twins were produced by an extramarital liaison, for which Zeus's wife Hera forbade Leto from giving birth anywhere on solid land.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Only the island of _____ allowed her to give birth to her children
Artemis.fact: Only the island of Delos allowed her to give birth to her children.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: She was worshipped and feared as one of the primary goddesses of childbirth and midwifery along with _____ and Hera
Artemis.fact: She was worshipped and feared as one of the primary goddesses of childbirth and midwifery along with Eileithyia and Hera.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: She was thought of as an unmarried maiden and one of the three Greek goddesses over whom _____ had no power
Artemis.fact: She was thought of as an unmarried maiden and one of the three Greek goddesses over whom Aphrodite had no power.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The hunter _____ was said to have seen her bathing naked, whereupon the goddess transformed him into a deer; he was then devoured by his own hunting dogs, who did not recognize their master
Artemis.fact: The hunter Actaeon was said to have seen her bathing naked, whereupon the goddess transformed him into a deer; he was then devoured by his own hunting dogs, who did not recognize their master.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Her great temple at _____ was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, before it was burnt to the ground
Artemis.fact: Her great temple at Ephesus was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, before it was burnt to the ground.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In later times, she was identified with _____, the personification of the Moon
Artemis.fact: In later times, she was identified with Selene, the personification of the Moon.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: According to J. T. _____, the name is also Phrygian and could be "compared with the royal appellation Artemas of Xenophon"
Artemis.fact: According to J. T. Jablonski, the name is also Phrygian and could be "compared with the royal appellation Artemas of Xenophon".

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: "butcher" or, like Plato did in Cratylus, to ἀρτεμής, _____, i.e
Artemis.fact: "butcher" or, like Plato did in Cratylus, to ἀρτεμής, artemḗs, i.e.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: 'the mistress of animals', a title associated with representations in art going back as far as the _____, showing a woman between a pair of animals
Artemis.fact: 'the mistress of animals', a title associated with representations in art going back as far as the Bronze Age, showing a woman between a pair of animals.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: "Potnia theron" is very close to the daimons and this differentiates her from the other _____ divinities
Artemis.fact: On a Greek vase from circa 570 BCE, a winged Artemis stands between a spotted panther and a deer. "Potnia theron" is very close to the daimons and this differentiates her from the other Greek divinities.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In some cults she retains the theriomorphic form of a Pre-_____ goddess who was conceived with the shape of a bear (άρκτος árktos: bear)
Artemis.fact: "Potnia theron" is very close to the daimons and this differentiates her from the other Greek divinities. In some cults she retains the theriomorphic form of a Pre-Greek goddess who was conceived with the shape of a bear (άρκτος árktos: bear).

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Laphria is the Pre-Greek "mistress of the animals" at _____ and Patras
Artemis.fact: Laphria is the Pre-Greek "mistress of the animals" at Delphi and Patras.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: She was worshipped with the surname _____ in several cities
Artemis.fact: She was worshipped with the surname Eucleia in several cities.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The goddess of vegetation was also related to the tree-cult with temples near the holy trees and the surnames _____, Caryatis and Cedreatis
Artemis.fact: The goddess of vegetation was also related to the tree-cult with temples near the holy trees and the surnames Apanchomene, Caryatis and Cedreatis.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: She was closely related to water and to _____, the god of the sea
Artemis.fact: She was closely related to water and to Poseidon, the god of the sea.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Her epithets include _____, Limnatis, Potamia, and Alphaea
Artemis.fact: Her epithets include Limnnaia, Limnatis, Potamia, and Alphaea.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In some cults, she is a healer goddess of women, bearing surnames such as Lousia and _____
Artemis.fact: In some cults, she is a healer goddess of women, bearing surnames such as Lousia and Thermia.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Some of the goddess's epithets were names of _____ like Lyceia or Molpadia
Artemis.fact: Some of the goddess's epithets were names of Amazons like Lyceia or Molpadia.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: An almost formulaic epithet used in the Iliad and _____ to describe her is ἰοχέαιρα iocheaira, "she who shoots arrows", often translated as "she who delights in arrows" or "she who showers arrows"
Artemis.fact: An almost formulaic epithet used in the Iliad and Odyssey to describe her is ἰοχέαιρα iocheaira, "she who shoots arrows", often translated as "she who delights in arrows" or "she who showers arrows".

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In European folklore, a wild hunter is said to chase an elfish woman who falls in the water; in _____ myth, the hunter chases a female deer and both disappear into the water
Artemis.fact: In European folklore, a wild hunter is said to chase an elfish woman who falls in the water; in Greek myth, the hunter chases a female deer and both disappear into the water. According to Greek beliefs the image of a god or a goddess gave signs or tokens and had divine and magic powers.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: According to _____ beliefs the image of a god or a goddess gave signs or tokens and had divine and magic powers
Artemis.fact: In European folklore, a wild hunter is said to chase an elfish woman who falls in the water; in Greek myth, the hunter chases a female deer and both disappear into the water. According to Greek beliefs the image of a god or a goddess gave signs or tokens and had divine and magic powers.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: With these conceptions she was worshipped as Tauria (the Tauric, goddess), _____ (Italy) and Anaitis (Lydia)
Artemis.fact: With these conceptions she was worshipped as Tauria (the Tauric, goddess), Aricina (Italy) and Anaitis (Lydia).

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In the bucolic (pastoral) songs the image of the goddess was discovered in bundles of leaves or dry sticks and she had the surnames _____ and Phakelitis
Artemis.fact: In the bucolic (pastoral) songs the image of the goddess was discovered in bundles of leaves or dry sticks and she had the surnames Lygodesma and Phakelitis.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: According to _____, she was born first, and assisted in the delivery of Apollo
Artemis.fact: According to Apollodorus, she was born first, and assisted in the delivery of Apollo.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: However, the local _____ peasants tried to prevent the twins and their mother from making use of the water by stirring up the muddy bottom of the spring, so the three of them could not drink it
Artemis.fact: However, the local Lycian peasants tried to prevent the twins and their mother from making use of the water by stirring up the muddy bottom of the spring, so the three of them could not drink it. Leto, in her anger that the impious Lycians had refused to offer hospitality to a fatigued mother and her thirsty infants, transformed them all into frogs, forever doomed to swim and hop around the spring.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The twins were quick to respond by raining down their arrows on _____, killing him
Artemis.fact: The twins were quick to respond by raining down their arrows on Tityos, killing him. For his actions against Leto, Tityos was banished to Tartarus, where he was pegged to the rock floor and stretched on an area of 9 acres (3.6 ha), while a pair of vultures feasted daily on his liver or his heart.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The twin sons of _____ and Iphimedeia, Otos and Ephialtes, known as the Aloadae, grew enormously at a young age
Artemis.fact: The twin sons of Poseidon and Iphimedeia, Otos and Ephialtes, called the Aloadae, grew enormously at a young age.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In another version, _____ sent the deer into the Aloadae's midst, causing their accidental killing of each other
Artemis.fact: In another version, Apollo sent the deer into the Aloadae's midst, causing their accidental killing of each other.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In another version, the _____ start piling up mountains to reach Mount Olympus, but the gods spot them and attack; once the twins had retreated, the gods learnt that Ares had been captured
Artemis.fact: The Aloadae threw their spears, mistakenly killing one another. In another version, Apollo sent the deer into the Aloadae's midst, causing their accidental killing of each other.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Unsure what to do with him, the _____ lock him up in a pot
Artemis.fact: Unsure what to do with him, the Aloedae lock him up in a pot.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Britomartis continually fled his advances, and to escape, she at last leapt into the sea (possibly from _____) and landed in fishermen's nets
Artemis.fact: Britomartis continually fled his advances, and to escape, she at last leapt into the sea (possibly from Mount Dikte) and landed in fishermen's nets.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: One day, Zeus pursued _____, who invoked her protectress, who in turn saved her from her father by turning her into the hind
Artemis.fact: The Cerynian hind used to be the Pleiad Taygete, called the "Mistress of Animals" and a dear companion of Artemis. One day, Zeus pursued Taygete, who invoked her protectress, who in turn saved her from her father by turning her into the hind.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Convinced by _____'s earnestness, she forgave him, foiling Eurystheus's plan
Artemis.fact: As Heracles was returning with the hind to present it to Eurystheus, he encountered Artemis and her brother Apollo. Convinced by Heracles's earnestness, she forgave him, foiling Eurystheus's plan.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Ancient artwork depicting the myth of _____ predate Aeschylus
Artemis.fact: In some surviving versions, though, Actaeon is a stranger who happens upon Artemis. A single line from Aeschylus's now lost play Toxotides ("female archers") is among the earlier attestations of Actaeon's myth, stating that "the dogs destroyed their master utterly", with no confirmation of Actaeon's metamorphosis or the god he offended (but it is heavily implied to be Artemis, due to the title).

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Diodorus also mentioned the alternative of _____ claiming to be a better hunter than the goddess of the hunt
Artemis.fact: Euripides, coming in a bit later, wrote in the Bacchae that Actaeon was torn to shreds and perhaps devoured by his "flesh-eating" hunting dogs when he claimed to be a better hunter than Artemis. In his Hymn to Athena, Callimachus writes that Actaeon chanced upon Artemis bathing in the woods, and she caused him to be devoured by his own hounds for the sacrilege, and he makes no mention of transformation into a deer either.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: This myth is very old; Homer knew of it and wrote that Niobe had given birth to twelve children, equally divided in six sons and six daughters (the _____)
Artemis.fact: This myth is very old; Homer knew of it and wrote that Niobe had given birth to twelve children, equally divided in six sons and six daughters (the Niobids).

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: While the sons were hunting in the woods, _____ crept up on them and slew all seven with his silver bow
Artemis.fact: Swiftly Apollo and Artemis descended on Thebes. While the sons were hunting in the woods, Apollo crept up on them and slew all seven with his silver bow.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Niobe wept for them, but did not relent, saying that even now she was better than _____, for she still had seven children, her daughters
Artemis.fact: Niobe wept for them, but did not relent, saying that even now she was better than Leto, for she still had seven children, her daughters.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In one version _____ died after pushing Leto out of the scorpion's way
Artemis.fact: Artemis then transferred him into the stars as the constellation Orion. In one version Orion died after pushing Leto out of the scorpion's way.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: She meant to marry him, and no talk from her brother _____ would change her mind
Artemis.fact: She meant to marry him, and no talk from her brother Apollo would change her mind. Apollo then decided to trick Artemis, and while Orion was off swimming in the sea, he pointed at him (barely a spot in the horizon) and wagered that Artemis could not hit that small "dot".

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: According to _____ in his lost poem Astronomia, Zeus appeared to Callisto, and seduced her, resulting in her becoming pregnant
Artemis.fact: According to Hesiod in his lost poem Astronomia, Zeus appeared to Callisto, and seduced her, resulting in her becoming pregnant.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Both of them were then captured by shepherds and given to Lycaon, and _____ thus lost her child
Artemis.fact: According to Hesiod in his lost poem Astronomia, Zeus appeared to Callisto, and seduced her, resulting in her becoming pregnant. Enraged, Artemis transformed Callisto into a bear, and in this form she gave birth to her son Arcas.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Sometime later, _____ "thought fit to go into" a forbidden sanctuary of Zeus, and was hunted by the Arcadians, her son among them
Artemis.fact: Enraged, Artemis transformed Callisto into a bear, and in this form she gave birth to her son Arcas. Both of them were then captured by shepherds and given to Lycaon, and Callisto thus lost her child.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: When she was about to be killed, _____ saved her by placing her in the heavens as a constellation of a bear
Artemis.fact: Sometime later, Callisto "thought fit to go into" a forbidden sanctuary of Zeus, and was hunted by the Arcadians, her son among them. When she was about to be killed, Zeus saved her by placing her in the heavens as a constellation of a bear.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In his De astronomia, _____, after recounting the version from Hesiod, presents several other alternative versions
Artemis.fact: In his De astronomia, Hyginus, after recounting the version from Hesiod, presents several other alternative versions. Hyginus then presents another version in which, after Zeus lay with Callisto, it was Hera who transformed her into a bear.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: This version also has both _____ and Arcas placed in the heavens, as the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor
Artemis.fact: The first, which he attributes to Amphis, says that Zeus seduced Callisto by disguising himself as Artemis during a hunting session, and that when Artemis found out that Callisto was pregnant, she replied saying that it was the goddess's fault, causing Artemis to transform her into a bear. This version also has both Callisto and Arcas placed in the heavens, as the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Hyginus then presents another version in which, after Zeus lay with _____, it was Hera who transformed her into a bear
Artemis.fact: The first, which he attributes to Amphis, says that Zeus seduced Callisto by disguising himself as Artemis during a hunting session, and that when Artemis found out that Callisto was pregnant, she replied saying that it was the goddess's fault, causing Artemis to transform her into a bear. This version also has both Callisto and Arcas placed in the heavens, as the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Hyginus also gives another version, in which Hera tries to catch Zeus and _____ in the act, causing Zeus to transform her into a bear
Artemis.fact: This version also has both Callisto and Arcas placed in the heavens, as the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor. Hyginus then presents another version in which, after Zeus lay with Callisto, it was Hera who transformed her into a bear.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Callisto is, rather than being transformed, simply ousted from the company of the huntresses, and she thus gives birth to _____ as a human
Artemis.fact: Callisto is, rather than being transformed, simply ousted from the company of the huntresses, and she thus gives birth to Arcas as a human. When Arcas, fully grown, is out hunting, he nearly kills his mother, who is saved only by Zeus placing her in the heavens.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Only later is she transformed into a bear, this time by _____
Artemis.fact: Hera, finding the bear, points it out to Artemis, who is hunting; Zeus, in panic, places Callisto in the heavens as a constellation. Only later is she transformed into a bear, this time by Hera.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: When Arcas, fully grown, is out hunting, he nearly kills his mother, who is saved only by _____ placing her in the heavens
Artemis.fact: Ovid gives a somewhat different version: Zeus seduced Callisto once again disguised as Artemis, but she seems to realise that it is not the real Artemis, and she thus does not blame Artemis when, during bathing, she is found out. When Arcas, fully grown, is out hunting, he nearly kills his mother, who is saved only by Zeus placing her in the heavens.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: He then turned her into a bear himself so as to hide the event from _____
Artemis.fact: Only later is she transformed into a bear, this time by Hera. He then turned her into a bear himself so as to hide the event from Hera.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Once Callisto was dead, _____ made her into a constellation, took the child, named him Arcas, and gave him to Maia, who raised him
Artemis.fact: In the Bibliotheca, a version is presented in which Zeus raped Callisto, "having assumed the likeness, as some say, of Artemis, or, as others say, of Apollo". Once Callisto was dead, Zeus made her into a constellation, took the child, named him Arcas, and gave him to Maia, who raised him.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Hermes was then sent by Zeus to take Arcas, and Zeus himself placed _____ in the heavens
Artemis.fact: Artemis then shot the bear, either upon the persuasion of Hera, or out of anger at Callisto for breaking her virginity. Once Callisto was dead, Zeus made her into a constellation, took the child, named him Arcas, and gave him to Maia, who raised him.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: In the hunt, _____ drew the first blood and was awarded the prize of the boar's hide
Artemis.fact: In some stories, Artemis later sent a bear to attack Atalanta because others claimed Atalanta was a superior hunter. Among other adventures, Atalanta participated in the Calydonian boar hunt, which Artemis had sent to destroy Calydon because King Oeneus had forgotten her at the harvest sacrifices.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: With the help of these dogs, _____ had been able to win the prize in the funeral games of Pelias
Artemis.fact: Cyrene was a fierce Thessalian huntress and companion of Artemis, who had given her two hunting dogs. With the help of these dogs, Cyrene had been able to win the prize in the funeral games of Pelias.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: After she killed the lion, he made her the new ruler of the lands, renamed _____ in her honor
Artemis.fact: Cyrene was a fierce Thessalian huntress and companion of Artemis, who had given her two hunting dogs. With the help of these dogs, Cyrene had been able to win the prize in the funeral games of Pelias.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: When King Eurypylus was still ruling Libya, a monstrous lion had terrorized the citizens greatly, so _____ brought Cyrene to get rid of it
Artemis.fact: When King Eurypylus was still ruling Libya, a monstrous lion had terrorized the citizens greatly, so Apollo brought Cyrene to get rid of it. In a story from Valerius Flaccus, Artemis and her mother Leto stood before Zeus with tearful eyes while Apollo pleaded with him to release Prometheus (the god who had stolen fire from the gods, given it to humans, and been chained in the Caucasus with an eagle feasting on his liver each day as punishment).

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Moved, Zeus agreed and commanded _____ to free Prometheus
Artemis.fact: Moved, Zeus agreed and commanded Heracles to free Prometheus.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Nemesis then arranges for Eros to make _____ fall in love with Aura
Artemis.fact: Nemesis then arranges for Eros to make Dionysus fall in love with Aura. Dionysus intoxicates Aura and rapes her as she lies unconscious, after which she becomes a deranged killer.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Dionysus intoxicates _____ and rapes her as she lies unconscious, after which she becomes a deranged killer
Artemis.fact: Nemesis agrees, telling Artemis that Aura's punishment will be to lose her virginity, since she dared question that of Artemis. Nemesis then arranges for Eros to make Dionysus fall in love with Aura.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Chione was a beautiful princess of _____
Artemis.fact: Chione was a beautiful princess of Phocis.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: As a punishment, _____ cursed her, causing her to mate and have children with a bear
Artemis.fact: Polyphonte was a young woman who fled home in pursuit of a free, virginal life with Artemis, as opposed to the conventional life of marriage and children favoured by Aphrodite. As a punishment, Aphrodite cursed her, causing her to mate and have children with a bear.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Her resulting offspring, _____ and Oreius, were wild cannibals who incurred the hatred of Zeus
Artemis.fact: Her resulting offspring, Agrius and Oreius, were wild cannibals who incurred the hatred of Zeus.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Coronis was a princess from _____ who became the lover of Apollo and fell pregnant
Artemis.fact: Coronis was a princess from Thessaly who became the lover of Apollo and fell pregnant.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: While Apollo was away, _____ began an affair with a mortal man named Ischys
Artemis.fact: Coronis was a princess from Thessaly who became the lover of Apollo and fell pregnant. While Apollo was away, Coronis began an affair with a mortal man named Ischys.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: The unborn child, _____, was later removed from his dead mother's womb
Artemis.fact: The unborn child, Asclepius, was later removed from his dead mother's womb.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Bellorophon was a divine Greek hero who killed the monster _____
Artemis.fact: Bellorophon was a divine Greek hero who killed the monster Chimera.

Artemis.subject: Education in India
Artemis.question: Apollo found him wounded by _____ and lifted him to heaven
Artemis.fact: Apollo found him wounded by Diomedes and lifted him to heaven.
